调节吹风机化油器时，先确认吹风管和喷口已安装，H、L 调节螺钉按基础设置旋至限位位置，并启动发动机预热。化油器有三颗调节螺钉：H 为高速油针，L 为低速油针，T 为怠速调节螺钉。<PIC> 调节低速油针 L 时，使发动机达到最高怠速转速后，再将 L 螺钉逆时针旋出最多 1/4 圈，并用 T 螺钉调整至稳定怠速；调节高速油针 H 时，全油门运行并调至最高转速后，再逆时针约 1/8 圈，注意全油门连续时间最长 10 秒，之后需怠速至少 10 秒。, ["Manual04_42"]

冷机启动吹风机时，先将停机开关调到“启动”位置，再将阻风门控制器调到阻风门位置 A，该位置同时也是自动启动油门位置；然后反复按压泵油膜片，直到燃油充满膜片即可，不需要完全充满。<PIC> 随后左手将机身按压在地面，右手握紧启动手柄，先缓慢拉到有阻力，再快速有力拉动。发动机点火后立即按下阻风门控制器，并重复拉动直到发动机启动；启动后迅速全开油门，启动油门会自动解除。<PIC> 注意不要完全拉出启动绳，也不要在启动绳完全拉出时松手。<PIC>, ["Manual04_25", "Manual04_28", "Manual04_26"]

热机启动吹风机时，先将停机开关调到“启动”位置；阻风门不要保持在冷机启动位置，而是先把阻风门控制器调到阻风门位置，再转回原位 B，这样只启用启动油门、不使用阻风门。然后按压泵油膜片，直到燃油充满膜片即可。<PIC> 接着左手固定机身，右手拉动启动手柄：先缓慢拉到有阻力，再快速有力拉动，直到发动机启动。启动后迅速全开油门，启动油门会自动解除。<PIC> 注意不要完全拉出启动绳，也不要在启动绳完全拉出时松手。<PIC>, ["Manual04_27", "Manual04_28", "Manual04_26"]
关闭吹风机时，请通过停机开关切断点火电源，使发动机停止运行。确认发动机完全停机、叶轮停止转动后，再放下设备或进行检查维护。<PIC>, ["Manual04_29"]
空调的重要组成部件包括室内机和室外机两部分。室内机通常包括前面板、空气滤网、3M多重防护滤网、等离子滤网、进风口、出风口、导风板和信号接收器等，具体功能会因机型不同而有所调整。<PIC> 室外机通常包括进风口、出风口、制冷剂管、排水管、连接线和底座板等，具体结构也可能因机型不同而调整。<PIC>, ["Manual01_0", "Manual01_1"]
空调无线遥控器的主要按键位于遥控器正面，部分附加功能按键位于遥控器盖板下方，打开盖板即可查看。使用遥控器时，请将遥控器对准空调底部的信号接收器；部分功能可能因机型不同而不支持。<PIC>, ["air_conditioner_01"]
给空调遥控器安装电池时，使用前请先装入 7 号电池。1 取下电池盖。<PIC> 2 装入新电池，确保电池正、负极安装正确。<PIC> 3 重新装上电池盖。 注 若遥控器显示屏开始变暗，请更换电池。, ["Manual01_2", "Manual01_3"]
安装空调遥控器支架时，应将支架固定在无阳光直射的位置，以保护遥控器。 1 选择安全且便于取用的位置。 2 用螺丝刀将两颗螺丝拧紧，固定支架。<PIC> 3 将遥控器滑入支架中。<PIC>, ["Manual01_4", "Manual01_5"]
用空调快速调节室内温度时，可使用极速制冷/制热模式；该模式可在夏季快速冷却室内空气，或在冬季快速提升室内温度。 1 按下开 / 关键开启电源。 2 按下极速键。<PIC> - 极速制冷模式下，空调将以 18 摄氏度的温度强风出风 30 分钟。 - 极速制热模式下，空调将以 30 摄氏度的温度强风出风 30 分钟。, ["Manual01_16"]
使用空调自清洁运行功能时，制冷和除湿运行产生的水汽可通过该功能去除。 1 按下自清洁键，显示屏上会显示自清洁标识。<PIC> - 若关闭电源，风扇将继续运行 30 分钟，对室内机内部进行清洁。 注 自清洁功能运行时，部分按键无法使用。, ["Manual01_17"]
使用空调等离子净化功能时，按下开/关键开启电源后，再按“等离子”键，显示屏会显示等离子标识，表示等离子净化运行已开启。部分机型也可以无需先开启空调，直接按等离子键使用；运行时等离子灯和制冷灯会同时亮起。注意：部分机型不支持该功能，请以您机器实际配置为准。<PIC>, ["Manual01_18"]
单冷型空调开启自动运行模式时，请先按开/关键开启电源，再反复按模式键选择“自动运行（人工智能模式）”。该模式下，风扇转速和温度会根据室内温度自动调节；如果当前温度高于或低于您希望的状态，可按上升/下降键选择对应的运行代码。需要注意的是，此模式下不能手动调节风扇转速，但可以设置导风板自动摆风，且部分机型可能不支持该功能。<PIC>, ["Manual01_19"]
使用空调自动转换运行功能时，该模式会自动切换运行模式，并将设定温度的波动控制在 2 摄氏度以内。 1 按下开 / 关键开启电源。 2 反复按下模式键，选择自动转换运行模式，显示屏上会显示对应标识。<PIC> 3 按下上升 / 下降键设置所需温度，温度调节范围为 18 摄氏度（64 华氏度）-30 摄氏度（86 华氏度）。 4 反复按下风速键选择风扇转速。, ["Manual01_20"]
开启节能制冷模式时，该模式可最大限度降低制冷耗电量，并将设定温度调节至较舒适水平。 1 按下开 / 关键开启电源。 2 反复按下模式键，选择制冷模式。 3 按下节能键，显示屏上会显示节能标识。<PIC>, ["Manual01_21"]

无遥控器时，可通过室内机的开/关键操作空调；此时风扇转速默认设为高速。 1 打开前盖板，轻轻掀起盖板两侧即可。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 2 按下开 / 关键。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 - 冷暖型机型的运行模式会根据室内温度自动切换。<PIC> - 单冷型机型的温度将默认设为 22 摄氏度（71.6 华氏度）。, ["Manual01_22", "Manual01_23", "Manual01_24"]

空调自动重启 停电后再次开启空调时，该功能可恢复之前的运行设置，此功能为工厂默认设置。 关闭自动重启功能 1 打开前盖板，轻轻掀起盖板两侧即可。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 2 按住开 / 关键 6 秒钟，设备会发出两声蜂鸣，指示灯闪烁 6 次。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 - 如需重新开启该功能，再次按住开 / 关键 6 秒钟即可，设备会发出两声蜂鸣，蓝色指示灯闪烁 4 次。, ["Manual01_25", "Manual01_26"]
不同型号空调的清洁频率应以维护保养表为准。一般情况下，空气滤网建议每两周清洁一次，必要时可增加清洁频率；3M多重防护滤网、等离子滤网等部件是否配备、清洁周期和清洁方式会因机型不同而不同。清洁前请关闭电源并拔下电源线，3M多重防护滤网切勿用水清洗，等离子滤网污垢较难清理时可用温水冲洗并阴干。<PIC>, ["Manual01_28"]

清洁空调空气滤网时，建议每两周清洁一次，必要时可增加清洁频率。 1 关闭电源并拔下电源线。 2 打开前盖板，轻轻掀起盖板两侧即可。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 3 握住空气滤网的把手，轻轻向上提起，将其从机身中取出。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 4 用吸尘器清理滤网，或用温水冲洗，若滤网污垢较难清理，可在温水中加入洗涤剂清洗。 5 将滤网置于阴凉处晾干。, ["Manual01_29", "Manual01_30"]
清洁空调 3M 多重防护滤网时， 1 关闭电源并拔下电源线。 2 打开前盖板，取出空气滤网（详见 “清洁空气滤网”）。 3 抽出 3M 多重防护滤网。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 4 用吸尘器清理滤网污垢，切勿用水清洗 3M 多重防护滤网，以免造成滤网损坏。 注 滤网的位置和形状可能因机型不同而有所差异。, ["Manual01_31"]
清洁空调等离子滤网时， 1 关闭电源并拔下电源线。 2 打开前盖板，取出空气滤网（详见 “清洁空气滤网”）。 3 在 10 秒内取下等离子滤网。<PIC> * 功能会根据机型有所调整。 4 用吸尘器清理滤网污垢，若污垢较难清理，可用温水冲洗。 5 将滤网置于阴凉处晾干。 注 ・滤网的位置可能因机型不同而有所差异。 ・部分机型可能未配备等离子滤网。, ["Manual01_32"]

快速组装蒸汽清洁机无需专用工具： 1. 将主机身固定扣（部件 15）从主机身（部件 7）背部取下。 2. 将主机身底部滑入旋转拖头（部件 18）颈部。<PIC> 图中主机身与旋转拖头背部的孔位已用白色标注以便识别。 3. 确保旋转拖头颈部背部的孔位与主机身孔位对齐。 4. 将主机身固定扣（部件 15）插入主机身背部孔位，将两部分锁紧。<PIC> 5. 按图示将手柄杆（部件 4）插入主机身（部件 7），直至听到咔嗒声到位。<PIC>, ["Manual05_3", "Manual05_4", "Manual05_5"]

蒸汽清洁机的实用功能包括：水箱位于手持蒸汽器顶部，可用蒸馏水或去离子水替代自来水；水过滤器可过滤矿物质和杂质；就绪指示灯亮起表示可使用；按下蒸汽开关或手持蒸汽器开关即可出蒸汽；旋转拖头便于清洁狭小空间和橱柜下方；吸水纤维拖布可吸附蒸汽松动的污垢并可机洗；喷嘴、圆刷、玻璃清洁组件等配件可用于不同清洁场景。<PIC> 快速上手时，先确认主机、拖头和手柄已装好；按下拖布释放扣并装入拖布。<PIC> 用量杯加水，或按水箱解锁扣取下水箱加水；不要加入除垢剂、芳香剂、酒精或洗涤剂。<PIC> 完全展开电源线并插入120V接地插座，待就绪指示灯亮起后按开关出蒸汽。<PIC>, ["Manual05_1", "Manual05_2", "Manual05_6", "Manual05_7"]
清洁硬质地面前请先扫地或吸尘。本机适用于瓷砖、乙烯基地板、复合地板、大理石、石材及封边木地板；不要用于未封边木地板，打蜡或部分未打蜡地面可能会降低光泽，建议先在不显眼处测试。使用时缓慢移动清洁机并按下蒸汽开关；如需消毒，可在目标区域停留至少15秒但不要超过20秒。若不出蒸汽，请拔下电源、取下水箱加水后再继续。首次使用时出蒸汽可能会延迟数秒，属于正常现象。
人体工学椅组装主要涉及配件包内的椅脚/底座、脚轮、气杆、底座盖、底盘、坐垫、椅背连接件、扶手、头枕、腰枕、脚踏及对应螺丝等部件。安装前建议先核对配件明细，再按图示依次安装脚轮、气杆、底盘、脚踏、椅背连接件、扶手、头枕和腰枕，最后确认各处螺丝已拧紧。<PIC>, ["Manual02_0"]
扶手使用一段时间后松动，通常是因为扶手和椅背的螺丝在日常使用过程中自然松动。按手册说明，重新拧紧扶手和椅背相关螺丝即可解决。<PIC>, ["Manual02_8"]

高度调节<PIC> 向上拉起 “升降” 拉杆即可调节椅子高度，到达所需高度后松开 “升降” 拉杆。调节高度时请将身体微微抬离座椅。<PIC> 椅背后仰功能<PIC> 向上拉起 “后仰” 拉杆，椅背角度可随人体动作独立倾斜。向下按下 “后仰” 拉杆，椅背角度即可锁定。将椅背复位至正常位置时请靠在椅背上，否则椅背可能会快速回弹。<PIC> 按摩功能 插入 USB 即可启用腰枕的按摩功能。<PIC>, ["Manual02_11", "Manual02_12", "Manual02_13", "Manual02_14", "Manual02_15"]
洗碗机部件包括： 1. 台式（视型号而定）2. 上层喷淋臂 3. 下层碗篮 4. 下层喷淋臂 5. 过滤器 6. 控制面板 7. 机门 8. 洗涤剂盒 9. 下层喷淋臂槽 10. 餐具篮 11. 专用盐箱盖 12. 上层篮导轨 13. 带支架的上层碗篮 14. 风扇烘干系统（视型号而定）<PIC>, ["Dish_washer_08"]
首次使用时，将洗碗机连接到排水口时，排水管可直接连接到排水孔或水槽排水口。 连接点距地面高度最小 50 厘米，最大 100 厘米。<PIC> 排水管长度超过 4 米会导致洗涤不干净。 将排水管平直连接到排水管，不得弯折。 牢固固定排水管，防止工作时脱落。 排水管必须连接到污水系统，不得连接到地表水。, ["Manual06_2"]

使用前为洗碗机添加专用盐时，软水系统需要再生以保持产品性能稳定，因此需使用洗碗机专用盐。 产品中只能使用洗碗机专用软化盐。 建议使用颗粒或粉末状软化盐。 请勿使用食盐等含不溶物的盐，否则软水系统性能会逐渐下降。 启动产品时盐箱会进水，因此请在启动机器前添加软化盐。 1. 先取出下层碗篮以便添加软化盐。 2. 逆时针旋转盐箱盖打开（A、B）。<PIC> 首次使用前，向软水系统注入 1 升水（C）。<PIC> 使用盐斗向盐箱加盐（D）。 为加速盐的溶解，可用勺子搅拌。<PIC> 盐箱约可装入 2 公斤软化盐。 4. 盐箱加满后盖上盖子并拧紧。 5. 若加盐后不立即启动洗涤程序，请空载运行最短程序，溶解并冲散机器内散落的盐。 由于市场上不同盐品牌的颗粒大小不同，且水硬度可能存在差异，盐在水中的溶解可能需要数小时。因此，加盐后盐量指示灯可能仍会亮一段时间。, ["Dish_washer_01", "Dish_washer_02", "Dish_washer_03"]

为洗碗机添加洗涤剂时，请参考程序表，根据所选程序确定正确的洗涤剂用量。 请勿向洗涤剂盒中加入溶剂，有爆炸危险！ 请按照下图所示，在即将运行机器前将洗涤剂加入洗涤剂盒。1. 向右推动卡扣打开洗涤剂盒盖（A）。<PIC> 2. 向洗涤剂盒中加入建议量的粉末或块状洗涤剂。 洗涤剂盒内有刻度标记，帮助您使用适量的洗涤剂。 洗涤剂盒装满容量为 40cm³。 根据机器装载量和 / 或餐具脏污程度，将洗涤剂加至 15cm³ 或 25cm³ 刻度线（1）。<PIC> 若餐具放置时间较长且残渣已干涸，可同时加满 5cm³ 小格（5）。 3. 轻轻按下关闭洗涤剂盒盖，听到咔嗒声表示已关紧。 在带预洗的高温程序中使用块状洗涤剂时，请确保洗涤剂盒盖紧闭。 无预洗的短程序建议使用粉末洗涤剂，因为块状洗涤剂的溶解度随温度和时间变化。 过量使用粉末洗涤剂会导致洗涤剂无法完全溶解，并在玻璃器皿上留下划痕。, ["Manual06_4", "Manual06_5"]

添加洗涤块时，先确保洗涤剂盒干燥，并在即将启动程序前加入。向右推动卡扣打开洗涤剂盒盖。<PIC> 按洗涤块包装说明，将洗涤块放入洗涤剂盒或指定位置，然后轻轻按下盒盖，听到“咔嗒”声后确认关紧。<PIC> 若机器带“洗涤块”功能，可在选择程序后按半载/洗涤块键启用，以改善多效洗涤块的烘干效果；无预洗短程序不推荐使用洗涤块，可改用粉末洗涤剂。, ["Manual06_4", "Manual06_6"]

在洗碗机中添加和使用亮碟剂时，应使用洗碗机专用亮碟剂；它可提高烘干效率，防止洗涤后的餐具上留下水渍或水垢。因此，务必确保亮碟剂盒中有亮碟剂，且仅使用洗碗机专用亮碟剂。 查看亮碟剂指示灯，判断是否需要添加亮碟剂（3）。指示灯常亮表示亮碟剂盒内充足，若指示灯熄灭则需添加。 1. 按下卡扣打开亮碟剂盒盖（B）。<PIC> 2. 向盒内加注至 MAX 刻度线。3. 轻轻按下关闭盒盖。 擦净溢出的亮碟剂。 意外溢出的亮碟剂会产生泡沫，最终降低洗涤效果。 4. 将亮碟剂剂量调节旋钮手动调至 1-6 之间的位置（4）。 若洗涤后餐具上有污渍，需调高剂量；若手擦后有蓝色痕迹，则调低剂量。出厂默认设置为 4。<PIC>, ["Manual06_7", "Manual06_8"]

不适合在洗碗机中清洗的物品・切勿在洗碗机中清洗沾有烟灰、蜡烛残渣、抛光剂、染料、化学品等的餐具。・请勿清洗铁制器具，以免生锈或在其他物品上留下污渍。・请勿清洗带有木质或骨质手柄、黏合部件、不耐热部件的银质餐具、刀具，以及铜和镀锡容器。 瓷器的装饰花纹以及铝制和银质器具在洗碗机中清洗后可能会褪色或失去光泽，就像手洗一样。 某些精致玻璃和水晶可能会逐渐失去光泽。强烈建议您在购买餐具时确认是否适合洗碗机清洗。
餐具篮为视型号而定的部件，用于更干净地清洗叉、勺等小件餐具。若您的型号配有餐具篮，可按图示将餐具篮放在对应位置后使用；尖锐刀叉应尖头朝下或水平放置，避免取放时受伤。<PIC>, ["Manual06_12"]
使用洗碗机前安装可折叠下层篮架时，可操作下层碗篮上的两根可折叠架丝（视型号而定），以便更方便地放置锅、碗等大件物品。 您可单独或同时折叠每根架丝以创造更大空间。按下卡扣（A）放下折叠架丝。<PIC>, ["Manual06_13"]

该功能视型号而定。满载时可调节的是上层碗篮高度，无需先取出餐具。升高时，抓住上层篮一侧架丝向上提起，另一侧重复相同操作；降低时，按下碗篮调节机构上的卡扣使碗篮下降，另一侧重复相同操作。调节后必须确认左右两侧处于同一水平。<PIC> 下层碗篮本身不做高度调节；如需在下层放置锅、碗等大件物品，可通过放下可折叠下层篮架丝来创造空间。<PIC>, ["Manual06_14", "Manual06_15"]
清洁洗碗机进水管滤网时，需先了解该滤网用于防止市政供水或自备水系统中的杂质（沙、污垢、铁锈等）损坏机器。 定期检查滤网和水管，必要时清洁。 1. 关闭水龙头并拆下水管。2. 取出滤网后在自来水下清洁。3. 将清洁后的滤网装回水管原位。 4. 将水管装回水龙头。<PIC>, ["Manual06_23"]
清洁洗碗机上层喷淋臂时，先检查上层喷淋臂（2）上的孔是否堵塞。 若堵塞，拆下并清洁喷淋臂。 向左旋转螺母拆下上层喷淋臂（C、D）。 安装上层喷淋臂时确保螺母拧紧。<PIC>, ["Manual06_24"]

拆除空气净化器滤网塑料包装前，务必拔下设备插头。双手握住设备上盖并向上拉起。<PIC> 握住背部滤网盖把手并向前拉出。<PIC> 拆除滤网上的塑料包装，未拆除包装会导致异响、滤网无法正常工作，甚至可能引发火灾或损坏设备。<PIC> 再将滤网上下推入设备并确保贴合紧密。<PIC> 装回滤网盖时，先将盖子插入设备底部固定卡槽，再向前滑动使其卡入顶部卡槽。<PIC> 最后双手握住设备上盖滑回原位，确保标识朝前。<PIC> 滤网安装完成后，长按控制面板上的“睡眠 + 自动”键5秒以上初始化，红色滤网指示灯熄灭即完成。注意：滤网塑料包装拆除后无法退货，塑料包装应远离儿童以防窒息。, ["Manual03_0", "Manual03_1", "Manual03_2", "Manual03_3", "Manual03_4", "Manual03_5"]
安装脚轮时，先从空气净化器包装盒内取出小盒，内含4个脚轮和8颗螺丝；再用螺丝刀拆下空气净化器底部四个底座；每个脚轮用两颗螺丝替换原底座并固定；最后保留拆下的底座和螺丝以备后续使用。若滤盒内无脚轮盒，请联系客服。

空气净化器主要有常规运行、自动运行、涡轮风扇运行和睡眠运行。常规运行下，按启动键开机后，通过控制面板上下键选择风速，可在F1至F18之间调节。<PIC> 自动运行下，按自动键在自动运行和常规运行之间切换，VOC传感器会检测室内空气质量并自动调节风速，智能自动运行期间不能手动调节风速。<PIC> 涡轮风扇运行下，需在常规运行模式下同时长按控制面板上下键3秒，可更快净化室内空气；按下控制面板下键后，风速将调至18档，涡轮风扇运行停止。<PIC> 睡眠运行下，按睡眠键进入，设备正常运行但显示屏熄灭，默认风速为1档，再按睡眠键可恢复之前模式，关机后睡眠模式取消。<PIC>, ["Manual03_14", "Manual03_15", "Manual03_16", "Manual03_17"]
室内空气质量（IAQ）指示灯用于实时查看室内空气质量，灯光环绕显示屏外缘。设备会根据检测到的细颗粒物浓度判断空气质量，并通过蓝、绿、黄、红四种颜色显示不同空气状态。需要注意的是，在门口、通风口、窗户等室外空气容易进入的位置，空气质量可能显示为更清洁的等级；该指示灯也可能对部分颗粒物无反应，读数可能与其他空气质量检测设备不同。<PIC>, ["Manual03_20"]
清洁设备内外前，请务必拔下电源插头。为保证最佳效果，建议每月清洁1-2次，灰尘较多地区可增加清洁频率。清洁外壳时，用温水或温和清洁剂浸湿的布擦拭净化器外壳，再用软布擦干。清洁内部时，打开背部滤网盖并取出滤网，用吸尘器和湿毛巾清洁滤网仓内部。
清洁滤网时，应根据滤网污染程度和使用环境调整处理方式。若滤网过脏，请直接更换。更换滤网期间，可用吸尘器或软刷清洁预过滤网。禁止用水清洗滤网，以免损坏滤网。

当滤网更换指示灯亮起红色时，需要更换滤网。<PIC> 通常建议每6-12个月更换一次，具体周期会因使用环境而异。更换前请拔下电源插头，不要在设备运行或通电状态下更换滤网。打开上盖。<PIC> 拉出背部滤网盖，取出旧滤网。<PIC> 新滤网安装前应拆除塑料包装。<PIC> 将新滤网上下推入设备并确保贴合紧密。<PIC> 装回滤网盖。<PIC> 再装回上盖。<PIC> 更换后，长按控制面板上的“睡眠 + 自动”键5秒以上重置滤网指示灯。, ["Manual03_21", "Manual03_0", "Manual03_1", "Manual03_2", "Manual03_3", "Manual03_4", "Manual03_5"]

清洁灰尘传感器前，请拔下电源插头。双手握住设备上盖并向上拉起。<PIC> 握住背部滤网盖把手并向前拉出。<PIC> 拆下设备右侧灰尘传感器盖。<PIC> 用蘸少量水的棉签擦拭灰尘传感器镜头和进风口，再用干净的干棉签彻底擦干。<PIC> 最后装回灰尘传感器盖、滤网盖，并将设备上盖标识朝前装回。注意不要使用丙酮、酒精等强腐蚀性化学试剂擦拭传感器部件，以免损坏镜头。, ["Manual03_22", "Manual03_23", "Manual03_24", "Manual03_25"]
长期存放空气净化器时，应在晴天让设备运行1小时，然后拔下电源插头，使设备内部晾干。之后遮盖设备，并存放在干燥、无阳光直射的地方。
这款健身单车的技术规格包括：<PIC> 最大使用者重量：136 千克（300 磅） 设备总占地面积：5670 平方厘米 机器重量：26.5 千克（58.4 磅）, ["Manual14_1"]

启动健身单车前，应先确认装配完成并完成最终检查，确保各部件紧固、机器放在坚固水平地面上，周围预留安全空间。然后连接交流电源适配器并接通电源。<PIC> 如机器不稳，应调节水平脚，使单车保持水平稳固。<PIC> 开始运动前还需调节座椅高度，使脚掌中心对准脚踏板中心、膝盖保持微弯，并确认锁销完全卡入且旋钮拧紧。<PIC> 最后将脚踏绑带固定在鞋面上，确保脚尖和膝盖朝前；阅读安全警告，确认未超过最大使用者重量136千克。<PIC>, ["Manual14_16", "Manual14_17", "Manual14_24", "Manual14_25"]

这款健身单车的控制台可提供运动重要信息，并可在运动时控制阻力等级。控制台配有带触控按键的显示屏，用于浏览运动程序。<PIC> 按键方面，阻力增加（♠）按钮——提高运动阻力等级；阻力减小（▼）按钮——降低运动阻力等级；快速启动按钮——开始快速启动运动模式；程序按钮——选择类别和运动程序；暂停/结束按钮——暂停当前运动、结束暂停运动或返回上一界面；目标追踪按钮——显示所选用户档案的运动总量与成就；增加（♠）/减小（▼）按钮——调节数值或浏览选项；左（◀）/右（▶）按钮——运动中切换运动数据或浏览选项；确认按钮——启动程序运动、确认信息或恢复暂停运动；风扇按钮——控制三速风扇；阻力等级快捷按钮——运动中快速切换阻力等级。显示功能包括上部显示数据/程序显示区<PIC> 和下部显示数据区<PIC> ，可查看速度、时间、距离、等级、RPM、心率、卡路里等运动数据。, ["Manual14_21", "Manual14_22", "exercise_bikes_02"]

运动前为了保证舒适度和安全性，主要需要调整座椅位置、脚踏绑带，并确认单车水平稳固。座椅高度应让脚踏板转到前位时，脚掌中心对准脚踏板中心，膝盖保持微弯；如果腿部过直或脚够不到脚踏板，就把座椅调低，如果膝盖弯曲过度，就把座椅调高。调节前请先下车，松开并拉出座管调节旋钮，调到合适高度后让锁销完全卡入并拧紧旋钮，不要超过STOP标记。<PIC> 脚部则将脚掌中心放在脚踏板上，把绑带固定在鞋面上，并确保脚尖和膝盖朝前。<PIC> 如单车不平稳，还应调节水平脚，确保机器稳定后再开始运动。<PIC>, ["Manual14_24", "Manual14_25", "Manual14_17"]
预设程序会自动控制不同阻力和运动等级，分为轻松骑行、山地、挑战等类别。轻松骑行类别包含：起伏山丘<PIC> 、公园骑行<PIC> 、轻松之旅<PIC>。, ["Manual14_27", "Manual14_28", "Manual14_29"]
预设程序会自动控制不同阻力和运动等级。山地类别包含：派克峰<PIC> 、胡德山<PIC> 、金字塔<PIC>。, ["Manual14_30", "Manual14_31", "Manual14_32"]
挑战类别属于更高难度预设程序，包含：上坡冲刺<PIC> 、交叉训练<PIC> 、间歇训练<PIC>。, ["Manual14_33", "Manual14_34", "Manual14_35"]

编辑健身单车用户档案前，先选择正确的用户档案；所有运动均保存到用户档案中。开始运动前请选择正确的用户档案。默认显示上次运动的用户。用户档案默认为默认值，可通过编辑自定义。请编辑用户档案以获得更准确的卡路里和心率信息。在开机模式界面，按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮选择一个用户档案。控制台将显示用户档案名称和图标。 编辑用户档案 1. 在开机模式界面，按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮选择一个用户档案。2. 按确认按钮选择用户档案。3. 控制台显示编辑提示和当前用户档案名称。按确认键开始编辑用户档案选项。如需退出编辑用户档案选项，按暂停/结束按钮，控制台返回开机模式界面。4. 控制台显示姓名提示和当前用户档案名称。注：首次编辑时用户姓名为空。用户档案名称限制为 10 个字符。当前激活段闪烁。使用增加/减少按钮浏览字母和空格（位于 A 和 Z 之间）。按左（◀）或右（▶）按钮切换段。按确认按钮接受显示的用户名。5. 编辑其他用户数据（编辑年龄、编辑体重、编辑身高、编辑性别），使用增加/减少按钮调节，每项设置完成后按确认键。6. 控制台显示扫描提示。此选项控制运动中运动数据的显示方式。“关闭”设置允许用户按需按左（◀）或右（▶）按钮查看其他运动数据通道。“开启”设置允许控制台每 6 秒自动切换显示运动数据通道。默认为“关闭”。按确认按钮设置运动数据显示方式。7. 控制台显示编辑下部显示提示。此选项允许自定义运动中显示的运动数据。下部显示区将显示所有运动数据，激活数据闪烁。上部显示区显示激活值设置：“开启”或“关闭”。按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮隐藏激活运动数据，按左（◀）或右（▶）按钮切换激活值。注：如需显示隐藏的运动数据，重复操作并将上部显示区数值改为“开启”。自定义下部显示完成后，按确认键设置。<PIC> 8. 控制台返回已选择用户的开机模式界面。, ["Manual14_26"]

在健身单车上设置心率目标时，可使用心率控制（HRC）运动程序；该程序可设置运动心率目标。程序通过本机接触式心率（CHR）传感器监测心率（次/分钟，BPM），调整运动强度以保持心率在所选区间。目标心率程序使用您的年龄和其他用户信息设置心率区间值。燃脂目标心率可参考按年龄显示的最大心率和目标心率区间图表。<PIC> 控制台显示屏将提示设置运动：1. 选择心率控制运动等级：初级（BEG）或高级（ADV），然后按确认键。2. 按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮选择最大心率百分比：50–60%、60–70%、70–80%、80–90%。80–90% 心率区间运动前请咨询医生。3. 按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮选择目标类型，然后按确认键。4. 按增加（♠）或减少（▼）按钮设置运动目标值。注：设置目标时请留出时间让心率达到目标区间。5. 按确认键开始运动。, ["Manual14_23"]

健身单车的体能测试程序用于评估体能水平提升。测试将功率输出（瓦特）与心率对比。体能提升后，相同心率下功率输出将增加。注：控制台必须能从接触式心率（CHR）传感器或心率监测仪（HRM）读取心率信息才能正常工作。可从反馈类别开始体能测试。体能测试程序首先提示选择体能水平——初级（BEG）或高级（ADV）。控制台将使用所选用户档案的年龄和体重计算体能得分。开始运动并握住心率传感器。测试开始后，运动强度逐渐增加，心率随之上升。强度持续自动增加，直至心率达到“测试区间”。该区间根据用户档案最大心率的 75% 单独计算。达到测试区间后，机器保持强度稳定 3 分钟，使您进入稳定状态（心率平稳）。3 分钟结束时，控制台测量心率和功率输出。结合年龄和体重信息计算得出“体能得分”。注：体能测试得分仅用于与自身历史得分对比，不与其他用户档案对比。对比得分查看体能提升。

拖曳速度是最低操控速度，几乎不加油门，艇体沉入水中且无尾流；适合靠岸、停靠码头或接近物体时的低速操控。<PIC> 半滑航速度是中等速度，艇首略微抬离水面但仍在水中行驶并产生尾流；适合练习中低速油门控制、大椭圆、绕圈和8字行驶。<PIC> 滑航速度是较快速度，艇体更平稳地在水面滑行并产生尾流；适合在开阔水域练习高速转向、停车距离判断和障碍物避让。速度越快，停车距离越长，转向也越需要油门动力。<PIC>, ["Manual40_1", "Manual40_2", "Manual40_3"]

先在近岸练习，再到开阔水域；练习时不要启动发动机，并在至少齐胸深的水域让艇漂浮。登艇时游至艇尾，双手放在登艇平台上，一手抓扶手。<PIC> 将身体拉到平台呈跪姿后移至座位跨坐。<PIC> 坐稳后将熄火绳系在手腕上并把卡扣装到熄火开关；双手握住车把，双脚放入脚坑，反复练习登艇和平衡。<PIC> 若配备登艇台阶，可放下辅助登艇，登艇后台阶会自动复位。<PIC>, ["Manual40_13", "Manual40_14", "Manual40_15", "Manual40_16"]

在滑航速度下转弯时，应先在开阔、平静、无交通和障碍物的大水域练习。转向需要油门，不能在试图转向时完全松开油门。先从较低速度和平缓转向开始，逐步提高速度和减小转弯半径。<PIC> 滑航速度下艇体在给定速度下的转向角度有限，车把转向过度时可能出现侧滑，导致无法更急转弯；此时应将车把转回较小角度，以恢复正常转向。可通过左右转向椭圆、圆圈与8字路线逐步练习。<PIC>, ["Manual40_26", "Manual40_27"]

要保持操控性和稳定性，应始终把油门与车把配合使用：除拖曳速度外，转向时必须保持油门，因为喷射推力强度决定转向速度和方向。练习时先逐渐加速到半滑航速度，保持速度平稳，先右转再左转，完成大椭圆。<PIC> 随后以稳定速度右转、左转绕大圈，并逐渐缩小圈径。<PIC> 最后结合前两项完成大8字路线，再逐步缩小8字尺寸。若松开油门，转向能力会迅速下降，艇体可能不再响应车把操作。<PIC>, ["Manual40_22", "Manual40_23", "Manual40_24"]
中低速转弯时，应把油门和车把配合使用。摩托艇通过车把改变尾部喷射推力喷嘴方向，从而改变行驶方向；除拖曳速度外，转向时必须保持油门，因为喷射推力强度决定转向速度和方向。可先逐渐加速到半滑航速度，保持速度平稳，再转动车把完成转向。急转弯时需要同时加大油门；如果松开油门，转向能力会迅速下降，艇体可能不再响应车把操作。<PIC>, ["Manual40_20"]

全加速后要安全停稳，先完全松开油门手柄，让发动机减速，艇体会因水阻逐渐减速，但仍会滑行一段距离才完全停止。从全速状态松油门或停止发动机后，完全停止距离约为90米（300英尺），具体受总重量、水面状况和风向影响。<PIC> 如配备RiDE，握紧RiDE手柄可缩短停车距离约30%，但仍不能当作规避危险的制动装置。若判断无法在障碍物前停下，应观察四周，加油门并转向避让。练习时应在开阔水域从较低速度开始，逐步提高最大速度。<PIC>, ["Manual40_21", "Manual40_25"]

设置日期和时间时，先按 + 或 - 调整年份，按“选择”键确认；再按 + 或 - 调整月份并确认，继续调整日期并确认。<PIC> 随后选择时钟格式，按 + 或 - 在12小时制和24小时制之间切换，按“选择”键确认。<PIC> 最后设置时间：按 + 或 - 调整小时并确认，再按 + 或 - 调整分钟并确认。完成后温控器即可按准确日期和时间执行程序日程与温度控制。<PIC>, ["Manual36_25", "thermostat_07", "Manual36_26"]

调整系统运行设置时，按“模式”键循环切换至所需系统模式并保持激活。可用模式包括：自动、供暖、制冷、应急供暖（仅适用于带辅助加热的热泵）和关闭；关闭模式下供暖/制冷系统关闭，但若风扇设为开启或循环，风扇仍可运行。由于压缩机保护，供暖/制冷指示灯可能会闪烁5分钟。<PIC> 调整风扇运行设置时，按“风扇”键循环切换至所需风扇模式并保持激活。风扇模式包括：自动（仅在供暖或制冷系统运行时启动）、开启（持续运行）和循环（随机运行约33%的时间）。<PIC>, ["Manual36_29", "Manual36_30"]

调整程序日程时，先按温控器上的“菜单”键，显示 PROG 后按“选择”；显示“开启”后再次按“选择”。<PIC> 然后按 + 或 - 选择要编辑的日期或日期组并确认；继续选择要编辑的日程时段（起床、离家、回家、睡眠）并确认。<PIC> 若该时段需要启用，显示“开启”时按“选择”；若要关闭该时段，按 + 后再按“选择”。随后按 + 或 - 调整该时段开始时间并确认。<PIC> 再依次调整供暖设定温度和制冷设定温度并确认；对剩余时段重复上述步骤，完成后按“主页”键保存程序设置并返回主界面。<PIC>, ["Manual36_31", "thermostat_04", "thermostat_05", "thermostat_06"]
可以使用“程序日程临时覆盖”。直接按温控器上的 + 或 - 键，将温度调整到所需设定值；调整后无需其他操作，新的设定温度会保持到下一个预定日程时段开始，原有程序日程不会被永久改动。若要提前取消临时覆盖，按 + 或 -，然后按“取消”键即可恢复原日程。<PIC>, ["Manual36_32"]

当主界面出现警报图标时，可在菜单中查看警报以了解错误或提醒代码。<PIC> 查看后，主界面会保留警报符号，直到警报被清除。<PIC> 进入警报菜单后，查看具体警报代码，并对照警报代码表判断问题。<PIC> 对于暂态警报，可选择 SNOOZE。<PIC> 取消后该警报会在7天后再次显示。<PIC> 若需要清除警报，可进入 CLEAR 界面执行清除。<PIC>, ["Manual36_44", "Manual36_45", "Manual36_46", "Manual36_47", "Manual36_48", "Manual36_49"]

热泵接线时，应先断开电源，并将每根已标记的电线与新温控器上相同字母的端子匹配，再把电线插入对应端子；如果插入困难，可按下端子旁的端子按钮。若需要使用热泵备用接线，请保持 R 滑动开关在向上位置（1根电线）。<PIC> 若旧温控器同时有 V 和 VR 电线，应立即停止并联系专业安装人员；若有单独的 O 和 B 电线，将 B 线连接至 C 端子，但如果 C 端子已连接其他电线，也应停止并联系专业安装人员；若旧温控器有 Y1、W1 和 W2 电线，同样应停止并联系专业安装人员协助。<PIC>, ["Manual36_35", "Manual36_36"]
温控器需电池供电。当电池低电量图标出现时，请立即更换新电池；该图标会在电池耗尽前约两个月显示。即使未出现低电量图标，也建议每年更换一次，或在离家超过一个月前更换。更换时建议使用AA碱性电池。若能在两分钟内完成电池更换，则无需重新设置时间和日期；其他设置会永久存储在内存中，不需要电池供电。<PIC>, ["Manual36_41"]

当常规系统标签与端子不匹配时，应按备用接线图处理。若必须同时连接 R 和 Rc 电线，将 R 滑动开关拨至向下位置（2根电线）。若旧温控器同时有 R 和 RH 电线，也将 R 滑动开关拨至向下位置，然后将 R 线连接至 Rc 端子、RH 线连接至 R 端子。若旧温控器只有1根 C 或 C1 电线，将其连接至 C 端子；若有2根 C 或 C1 电线，应分别用电工胶带包裹且不连接。完成后确认每根电线插入对应端子并固定牢靠。<PIC>, ["Manual36_34"]

遇到温控器故障时，可按手册逐项排查：若屏幕空白并使用电池供电，请确认已正确安装全新AA碱性电池；若无法将系统设置切换至制冷模式，检查系统设置选项220是否设为1或2；若需要供暖时风扇不启动，检查系统设置选项205是否与供暖设备匹配；若制冷模式下供暖系统运行，检查系统设置选项200或218是否与供暖和制冷设备匹配；若供暖或制冷系统无响应，先将系统设置为供暖或制冷并确认设定温度高于或低于室内温度，再检查断路器、系统电源开关和炉门是否关闭，并等待5分钟响应；若屏幕上“供暖开启/制冷开启”闪烁，说明压缩机保护已启动，等待5分钟让系统安全重启；若热泵供暖吹冷风或制冷吹热风，检查系统设置选项200或218是否正确。安装或拆卸前注意断开电源，避免触电或设备损坏。<PIC>, ["Manual36_50"]
处理器单元包括正面的状态指示灯（白色为已开机，红色为待机模式）、AUX端口和HDMI输出端口。<PIC> 背面包括HDMI电视端口、HDMI PS4端口、USB端口、DC IN 12V接口和通风口。<PIC>, ["Manual38_1", "Manual38_2"]
手册中对应的是立体声耳机，耳塞出厂默认安装M号，也可更换为S号或L号以获得更贴合的佩戴效果。<PIC> 更换时，旋转耳塞并将其拔下，再换上合适尺寸耳塞；安装时应确保耳塞牢固，避免使用过程中意外脱落。<PIC>, ["Manual38_3", "Manual38_4"]
清洁遮光罩时，先将遮光罩从VR头显上取下，用水清洗；再用软布完全擦干后装回头显。重新安装时，将遮光罩上的凸点与头显上的13个孔对齐。清洁前应拔下电源线并断开其他线缆，且不要使用溶剂或其他化学药剂。<PIC>, ["Manual38_5"]
为获得安全且较佳的PS VR体验，应在摄像头捕捉范围内使用。游玩区域约为宽3.0米（9.8英尺）、深1.9米（6.2英尺），高度取决于摄像头捕捉范围。使用前请清理大于游玩区域的活动空间，并按PS VR设置界面调整摄像头位置和角度，使自己位于游玩区域中央。<PIC>, ["Manual38_0"]

使用和操作VR头显时，应注意：1）12岁以下儿童不适用；疲劳、头晕、恶心、醉酒、服药、平衡感受损或患有严重疾病时不要使用，必要时先咨询医生。2）使用前清理大于游玩区域的活动空间，远离墙壁、楼梯、家具等障碍物，并防止宠物或他人进入。3）佩戴时尽量保持坐姿，站立模式需按应用指示操作，避免剧烈动作；开始前和使用中检查线缆是否缠绕身体或四肢。4）若出现头晕、视觉异常、抽搐、意识丧失、恶心、头痛等症状，应立即停止使用并休息，必要时就医。5）通常每游玩1小时休息15分钟，初次使用建议短时间体验。6）为保护设备，不要抓着线缆甩动头显或电源适配器；待追踪灯熄灭后再取下头显或拔下连接线；不要让液体或细小颗粒进入接口、通风口等位置；不要遮挡处理器单元通风口；发现异常声音、气味或过热时立即停止使用并断开电源。7）清洁前拔下电源线并断开所有线缆，不使用溶剂或其他化学药剂。

设置功能键盘时，先将USB-C线连接到键盘并接入电脑。<PIC> 如果使用腕托，将磁吸腕托吸附到键盘前侧对应位置。<PIC> 需要调整输入角度时，可展开键盘底部支撑脚；完成连接后即可按需在CAM中设置灯光、宏命令、按键重映射或板载配置文件。<PIC>, ["function_keyboard_02", "Manual21_3", "Manual21_11"]
拆卸功能键盘轴体时，使用附赠拔轴器从顶部夹住轴体，将工具两端沿轴体前后方向放置，按下轴体两侧卡扣后向上拔出，注意不要刮擦上盖面板，也不需要从轴体下方撬动。<PIC> 重新安装轴体前，先确认轴体针脚平直并与PCB插孔对齐，再垂直向下按入定位板，确认轴体固定到位后再装回键帽。<PIC>, ["Manual21_14", "Manual21_15"]

使用功能键盘搭配 CAM 软件时，先前往官网下载并安装最新版 CAM 软件。然后在 CAM 中设置键盘配置文件并保存到键盘，本键盘自带四个板载配置文件，保存后无需运行 CAM 也可使用已存储的灯光、宏命令等功能。<PIC> 按 FN+F1/F2/F3/F4 可切换到对应 1-4 号配置文件；还可在 CAM 的键盘/灯光界面逐键自定义 RGB 灯光，在宏命令界面创建宏，在按键重映射界面创建新的自定义按键绑定。<PIC>, ["Manual21_7", "Manual21_8"]
硬件模式下使用键盘时，可直接通过快捷键调用板载配置。配置文件1至4自带四种默认灯光模式，按 FN+F1、FN+F2、FN+F3 或 FN+F4 可切换至对应配置文件。<PIC> 如果已将自定义灯光保存到板载配置文件，切换到该配置文件时会直接启用自定义灯光，不需要保持 CAM 软件运行。<PIC>, ["Manual21_7", "Manual21_10"]

安装儿童电动摩托车挡泥板时，应由成人完成组装，并让儿童远离小部件。先将挡泥板侧转并向上滑入左侧把手管，注意不要卡入1号孔。<PIC> 再使挡泥板凸点卡入2号孔。<PIC> 如继续安装右侧把手管，应让右侧把手管穿过把手固定夹和挡泥板，并用M6×50螺栓和M6螺母固定。<PIC>, ["rideon_motorcycle_01", "rideon_motorcycle_02", "Manual26_5"]

安装儿童电动摩托车前轮时，按图示将前轴穿过两侧把手管及前轮，两侧把手管内外均需安装垫片。<PIC> 再使用两个螺母将前轴和车轮固定在把手管上，并用随产品提供的扳手拧紧螺母直至螺纹尽头。<PIC> 前轮及前轴组装完成后，还要检查车轮与把手管之间的间隙；若间隙过大或车轮定位不稳，可在车轮与把手管之间加装额外垫片（不随产品提供）。重新安装后应确保间隙最小化且车轮可自由转动，若车轮卡死则减少一片垫片。, ["Manual26_6", "Manual26_7"]
为蓝牙激光鼠标安装电池时，需要使用两节 AA 电池。先按下按钮，使电池仓盖弹出。<PIC> 然后按照鼠标内部标注的正负极（+ 和 -）装入两节 AA 电池。<PIC> 最后装回电池仓盖。<PIC>, ["Manual27_1", "Manual27_2", "Manual27_3"]

安装 WIDCOMM 蓝牙驱动程序前，请先将 USB 蓝牙接收器插入电脑的 USB 接口。然后将附带的安装光盘放入光驱，驱动程序会自动加载；若未自动加载，请双击光驱中 bin 文件夹内的 Setup.exe。欢迎界面出现后点击“下一步”继续。<PIC> 阅读协议并选择“我接受许可协议中的条款”，再点击“下一步”。<PIC> 确认安装文件夹，必要时点击“更改”选择其他路径，然后点击“下一步”。<PIC> 点击“安装”开始安装，安装过程可能需要一些时间。<PIC> 出现完成界面表示安装结束。<PIC> 最后拔下接收器并重新插入，鼠标将自动配对；点击“完成”退出安装。系统提示重启电脑时，可点击“是”立即重启，或点击“否”稍后重启。<PIC>, ["Manual27_4", "Manual27_5", "Manual27_6", "Manual27_7", "Manual27_8", "Manual27_9"]
卸载 WIDCOMM 蓝牙驱动程序时，先拔下 USB 蓝牙接收器；然后依次点击“开始 > 设置 > 控制面板 > 添加或删除程序”；在程序列表中选择 WIDCOMM 蓝牙软件并点击“删除”。系统会开始卸载程序，此过程可能需要一些时间。卸载完成后，系统会提示重启电脑，可点击“是”立即重启，或点击“否”稍后重启。

在 Windows 系统中为蓝牙激光鼠标快速配对时，先将 USB 蓝牙接收器插入电脑的 USB 接口；然后按下鼠标底部的配对按钮。配对按钮位置如图所示。<PIC> 再按下 USB 蓝牙接收器底部的按钮，直至 LED 指示灯每秒闪烁一次，表示蓝牙接收器已开始搜索待配对设备（本款鼠标不含接收器销售）。<PIC> 最后移动鼠标，确认连接成功。, ["Manual27_10", "Manual27_11"]
通过 WIDCOMM 蓝牙驱动程序为蓝牙激光鼠标配对前，应先按手册中 WIDCOMM 蓝牙驱动程序安装说明完成驱动安装。配对时，按下 USB 蓝牙接收器按钮，直到出现人机接口设备（HID）界面。<PIC> 鼠标连接成功后，会出现确认信息；点击确认连接正确的鼠标。<PIC>, ["Manual27_12", "Manual27_13"]

拆卸烤箱门 拆卸门体：1. 完全打开烤箱门。2. 抬起卡扣并向前推至极限位置（图1）。<PIC> 3. 将烤箱门关至最大角度（A），向上抬起（B）并转动（C）直至脱开（D）（图2）。<PIC>, ["oven_01", "oven_02"]

"Battery switches The batteries and switch assembly are located in the battery compartment. This boat uses two marine batteries. One battery is designated as the start battery. The start battery is connected to the starter circuit on the engine to provide current for the starter motor. The other battery is designated as the house battery. The house battery provides power for the various accessory circuits on the boat, such as the circuits for the lighting, bilge pump, blowers and audio system. 1 Battery switch assembly 2 Start battery 3 House battery <PIC> There are three switches on the battery switch assembly: the “START” switch, “HOUSE” switch, and “EMERG PARALLEL” switch. 1 “HOUSE” switch (red) 2 “EMERG PARALLEL” switch (yellow) 3 “START” switch (red) <PIC> 1 ON position (green) 2 OFF position (red) <PIC> In normal operation, keep the “START” and “HOUSE” switches in the ON position. Keep the “EMERG PARALLEL” switch in the OFF position. This setting allows both batteries to be charged automatically while the engine is running. NOTICE: Do not turn the “HOUSE” switch to the OFF position if the boat is moored in the water as it will prevent the anchor light from functioning. If the start battery is discharged, turn the “EMERG PARALLEL” switch to the ON position to start the engine. Once the engine is started or the start battery is charged, turn the “EMERG PARALLEL” switch to the OFF position.", ["Manual09_42", "Manual09_43", "Manual09_44"]

"Steering. The boat steers by water-jet thrust: turning the steering wheel changes the angle of the jet thrust nozzles at the rear of the boat, and the stern responds first. Keep throttle applied while turning, because jet thrust determines steering force; if the remote control levers are pulled back to idle, steering ability decreases rapidly. <PIC> The articulating keel follows the movement of the jet thrust nozzles and helps the boat change direction. Allow extra clearance near docks, swimmers, obstacles or other boats because the boat turns from the stern. <PIC>", ["Manual09_52", "Manual09_53"]

"Over temperature warning. If the engines start to overheat, the multifunction display shows an over-temperature warning and the buzzer sounds; engine speed is automatically limited to help prevent damage. Immediately reduce engine speed, return to shore or maneuver to a safe location, and check cooling-water discharge. <PIC> The cooling-water pilot outlets are on the starboard side of the hull; confirm that water is coming out while the engines are running, especially while applying throttle. If no water comes out, cooling water may not be circulating properly. <PIC>", ["Manual09_95", "Manual09_96"]

"Engine oil level check. Keep the boat precisely level. If checking on land, supply water to the cooling-water passages while the engines run; if checking on water, moor the boat so it will not drift. Start the engine, run it at idle for 6 minutes or more, then stop it. Open the engine hood and remove the oil tank filler cap/dipstick. <PIC> Wipe the dipstick clean, screw it fully back in, remove it again, and check that the oil level is between the minimum and maximum marks. Add oil slowly if below minimum; consult a dealer if it is significantly above maximum. Repeat for the other engine and close the hood. <PIC>", ["Manual09_196", "Manual09_197"]

"Starting the boat engines. "Turning the boat WARNING  Do not pull the remote control levers back to idle when trying to steer away from objects — you need throttle to steer.  Be sure passengers are holding on before making turns. An unprepared passenger could lose balance and fall. Steering control depends on the combination of steering wheel position and the amount of throttle. Water sucked in through the intake grate is pressurized by the impeller in the jet pumps. As the pressurized water is expelled from the pumps through the jet thrust nozzles, it creates thrust to move and steer the boat. The higher the engine speed, the more thrust is produced. The amount of jet thrust, in addition to the position of the steering wheel, determines how sharply you turn. A. More throttle produces high thrust, so the boat will turn more sharply. <PIC> B. Less throttle produces low thrust, so the boat will turn more gradually. <PIC> C. Pulling the remote control levers back to idle or neutral position produces only minimum thrust. If you are traveling at speeds above trolling, you will have rapidly decreasing ability to steer without throttle. You may still have some turning ability immediately after pulling the remote control levers back to idle, but when the engines slows down, the boat will no longer respond to steering wheel input until you apply throttle again or you reach a trolling speed. At trolling speed, the boat can be turned gradually by steering wheel position alone using just the amount of thrust available at engine idle. <PIC> D. If the boat is moving and the remote control levers are in neutral position, or if there is no thrust because the engines are stopped, the boat will go straight even though the steering wheel is turned.", ["Manual09_239", "Manual09_240", "Manual09_241"]

"Crossing wakes and swells. Do not take wakes or swells straight on at high speed. Reduce speed and change your crossing angle so the jolt is smaller; crossing at an angle is usually smoother than hitting the wake squarely. <PIC> Be prepared for the boat to try to turn away from the wake or swell, especially at small crossing angles such as about 10 degrees. Adjust speed and angle before crossing large, sharp wakes or broad swells. <PIC>", ["Manual09_249", "Manual09_250"]

"Loading (1) Disconnect the trailer lights from the towing vehicle. (2) Back the trailer down the ramp as close to 90 to the shoreline as you can. If possible, have a second person act as an observer while standing to the side of the trailer. Stop when the tops of the trailer’s fenders are about 3 inches above the waterline. (3) With the boat moving at the slowest idle speed, guide the boat onto the support rails. Use throttle only if necessary for steering ability. WARNING! Using too much throttle can cause the boat to jump over the front of the trailer, which can result in injury to the boat operator and bystanders. (4) Make sure the boat is centered on the support rails and is headed straight for the bow stop (bumper board). Ease the boat forward until the bow rests against the bow stop. NOTICE: The winch line is not designed to pull the boat onto the trailer. (5) Attach and tighten the winch line. NOTICE: The winch line should not be the only line securing the bow during trailering. Use the chain along with the winch to secure the boat to the trailer. <PIC> 1 Bow eye(6) Pull the trailer up the ramp out of the way of other boaters. Attach the bow and stern tie-downs. Reconnect the trailer lights. <PIC> 1 Stern eye (7) Perform the post-operation checks on page 105.", ["Manual09_255", "Manual09_256"]

"Flushing the cooling system Cooling system flushing is essential to prevent the cooling system from clogging up with salt, sand, or dirt. (1) Connect the garden hose adapter to a garden hose. <PIC> 1 Garden hose adapter 2 Garden hose (2) Loosen the flush hose connector cap and remove it. Insert the garden hose adapter into the flush hose connector by pushing and twisting it until it is securely connected. <PIC> 1 Flush hose connector 2 Flush hose connector cap 3 Garden hose adapter (3) Connect the garden hose to a water tap. (4) Make sure that the area around the boat is clear, and then start the engine. Immediately after the engine starts, fully turn the water supply on so that water flows out continually from the jet thrust nozzle and cooling water pilot outlet. NOTICE: Never turn on the water before starting the engine. The water could flow back through the muffler into the crankcase causing severe engine damage. Be sure to turn on the water immediately after starting the engine to prevent engine overheating. (5) Run the engine at a fast idle for 3 to 5 minutes. If the engine stops while flushing, turn the water supply off immediately and perform the procedure again from step 4. (6) Turn off the water supply, and then drain residual water from the exhaust system by alternately pushing the remote control lever up to half throttle and back to idle for 10 to 15 seconds. (7) Stop the engine. NOTICE: Never have the water on when the engine is not running. The water could flow back through the muffler into the crankcase causing severe engine damage. Do not run the engine for more than 15 seconds after the water supply has been turned off to avoid engine overheating. (8) Remove the garden hose adapter.(9) Install and tighten the cap securely.", ["Manual09_257", "Manual09_258"]

"WARNING Do not use fuses of a higher amperage than recommended. Substitution with a fuse that has an improper rating can cause extensive electrical system damage and possible fire. If a fuse is blown, replace it with the proper fuse. To replace a fuse:(1) Open the engine hood. (See page 56.)(2) Unfasten the band. <PIC> 1 Band (3) Remove the fuse box from the air filter case by pulling the fuse box toward the bow. (4) While pushing both sides of the fuse box cover inward, pull the cover toward the bow and remove it. <PIC> 1 Fuse box cover <PIC> 1 Electronic throttle valve fuse 2 Fuel pump fuse 3 Main relay drive fuse 4 Main fuse 5 Fuse puller 6 Battery fuse 7 Spare fuse 8 Unused fuse (5) When replacing the accessory fuse and bilge pump fuse, remove the fuse holder. (Open the battery compartment to access the accessory fuse and bilge pump fuse. [See page 66.]) <PIC> 1 Fuse holder 2 Accessary fuse 3 Bilge pump fuse (6) Replace the blown fuse with the spare fuse of the correct amperage by using the fuse puller. Towing the boat Fuse amperage: Electronic throttle valve fuse: 10 A Fuel pump fuse: 10 A Main relay drive fuse: 10 A Main fuse: 20 A Battery fuse: 30 A Accessory fuse: 20 A Bilge pump fuse: 3 A (7) Install the fuse box cover.(8) If the accessory fuse or bilge pump fuse was replaced, install the fuse holder.(9) Install the fuse box to the air filter case.(10) Fasten the band.(11) Close the engine hood.", ["Manual09_281", "Manual09_282", "Manual09_283", "Manual09_284"]

"Engine oil level check. Keep the boat precisely level; if checking on land, supply water to the cooling-water passages while the engines are running, and if checking on water, moor the boat so it will not drift. Start the engine, run it at idle for 6 minutes or more, then stop it. Open the engine hood, remove the oil tank filler cap/dipstick, wipe the dipstick clean, screw it fully back in, and remove it again. <PIC> Confirm that the oil level is between the minimum and maximum marks. Add oil slowly if below minimum; consult a Yamaha dealer if it is significantly above maximum. Repeat for the other engine and close the engine hood. <PIC>", ["Manual09_196", "Manual09_197"]

"Energy-saving mode. The coffee machine automatically enters power-off mode after 9 minutes of non-use. To turn it on again, press either the Espresso button or the Lungo button. <PIC> To turn the machine off manually before the automatic power-off time, press the Espresso and Lungo buttons at the same time. <PIC>", ["Manual07_4", "Manual07_5"]

"Changing the default energy-saving setting. With the machine turned off, press and hold the Espresso button for 3 seconds; the Espresso button blinks to indicate the current setting. <PIC> Press the Espresso button once to select automatic power-off after 9 minutes. <PIC> Press it again to select automatic power-off after 30 minutes. <PIC> Press it once more to deactivate automatic power-off, then press and hold the Lungo button for 3 seconds to exit and save the setting. <PIC>", ["Manual07_6", "Manual07_7", "Manual07_8", "Manual07_9"]

"Programming water volume. Turn the coffee machine on and wait until it is ready, with steady lights. <PIC> Fill the water tank with potable water, insert a capsule, and place a cup under the coffee outlet. <PIC> Press and hold the Espresso or Lungo button to start programming that cup size. <PIC> Release the button when the desired coffee volume has been served; the new water volume is stored for that button. <PIC>", ["Manual07_24", "Manual07_25", "Manual07_26", "Manual07_27"]

"To empty the system before non-use, frost protection, or repair, press both Espresso and Lungo buttons to turn the machine off. <PIC> Remove the water tank and open the lever, then press both buttons for 3 seconds until both LEDs blink alternately. <PIC> Close the lever; the machine switches off automatically. <PIC> Empty and clean the used capsule container and drip tray. <PIC> The machine is blocked for 10 minutes after emptying mode. <PIC>", ["Manual07_28", "Manual07_29", "Manual07_30", "Manual07_31", "Manual07_32"]

"To reset to factory settings, make sure the machine is turned off, then press and hold the Lungo button for 5 seconds. <PIC> The LEDs blink fast 3 times to confirm reset, then continue blinking normally during heat-up until steady lights show the machine is ready. <PIC> Factory settings are Espresso cup 40 ml, Lungo cup 110 ml, and power-off mode after 9 minutes. <PIC>", ["Manual07_33", "Manual07_34", "Manual07_35"]

"For cleaning, unplug the machine and let it cool. <PIC> Never immerse the appliance or any part of it in water, do not use strong cleaning agents, solvents, sharp objects, brushes, abrasives, or a dishwasher. <PIC> Clean the coffee outlet regularly with a soft damp cloth, and remove the maintenance unit in separate pieces for easy cleaning.", ["Manual07_47", "Manual07_48"]

"Swim platform and ladder. The swim platform is the rear boarding/sitting area; stay away from it while the engines are running because exhaust gases can collect there. <PIC> To use the ladder stored under the swim platform, lift the end of the ladder to release it from the hooks, pull it out completely, and lower it. <PIC> To stow the ladder, raise it until horizontal, push it forward completely, and press the end back onto the hooks. <PIC>", ["Manual09_168", "Manual09_169", "Manual09_170"]

"Livewell The livewell for holding live bait and fish is located on the starboard side of the boat at the stern. To open the livewell: Pull the latch to open the livewell lid. <PIC> 1 Livewell lid 2 Latch <PIC> 1 Livewell To supply water to the livewell: (1) Push the livewell switch to turn on the livewell pump and supply water. (2) When there is sufficient water in the livewell, push the livewell switch to turn off the livewell pump. (3) If necessary, push the aerator switch to aerate and circulate the water in the livewell. (See page 52.) <PIC> 1 Aerator switch 2 Livewell switch", ["Manual09_153", "Manual09_154", "Manual09_155"]

"The maintenance setting screen shows the number of hours the engines have been running since the last maintenance. After maintenance is performed, reset the operating-hour counter by tapping the “Reset” button; when the confirmation message appears, tap “YES” to reset the hours. If you want to return without resetting, tap “NO.” <PIC>", ["Manual09_83"]

"Factory reset screen This screen can be used to reset the settings to their factory default settings. <PIC> To reset the settings: (1) Tap the “Reset” button. <PIC> 1 “Reset” button (2) When the confirmation message appears, tap the “YES” button to reset the settings. TIP: To return to the factory reset screen without resetting the settings, tap the “NO” button. <PIC> 1 “YES” button", ["Manual09_87", "Manual09_88", "Manual09_89"]

"Trip screen. The trip screen displays engine-operation hours, fuel consumption and other trip information. The screen includes the menu, scrollbar and Reset button. <PIC> The menu displays 4 items at one time, and you scroll through the menu items using the scrollbar. <PIC> Items marked with an asterisk cannot be reset. To reset one item, touch and hold that item for several seconds; to reset all resettable display items, tap the Reset button.", ["Manual09_69", "Manual09_70"]

"To make the boat move forward after the engines are started and the area is clear, move the remote control levers from neutral into the forward position. In forward, the shift gates are lifted all the way up and the jet thrust is directed to the rear, which moves the boat forward. Apply throttle gradually and keep watch for people or obstacles; the boat is jet-propelled, so steering response depends on jet thrust and will be weak if the levers are pulled back to idle. <PIC>", ["Manual09_49"]

"Steering system checks Make sure the steering wheel is not loose. There should not be any free play, either inand-out or in rotation. Turn the steering wheel fully to the right and left to make sure operation is smooth and unrestricted throughout the whole range. <PIC> Make sure both the jet thrust nozzles change directions as the steering wheel is turned. The jet thrust nozzles should point to starboard (right) when the wheel is turned to the right. The jet thrust nozzles should point to port (left) when the wheel is turned to the left. There should not be free play between the steering wheel and the jet thrust nozzles. In addition, check that the direction of the articulating keel changes according to the movement of the jet thrust nozzles. <PIC> 1 Jet thrust nozzle 2 Articulating keel Remote control lever checks WARNING Do not touch the shift gates while the remote control levers are being operated, otherwise, you could be pinched. Operate the remote control levers several times to make sure that operation is smooth throughout the whole range. 1 Neutral position 2 TDE position 3 Forward position 4 Reverse position 5 Shift 6 Fully closed 7 Throttle 8 Fully open Check that the shift gates are slightly above the shift gate neutral position when the remote control levers are in the forward position, and that the shift gates are in the fully open position when the remote control levers are moved farther forward. Fully open position Check that the shift gates are in the fully closed position when the remote control levers are in the reverse position. Fully closed position 1 Shift gate", ["Manual09_206", "Manual09_207"]

"Fire extinguisher storage/check. As an inboard boat less than 26 feet long, the boat must carry one 5-B (B-1) type fire extinguisher when navigating U.S. Coast Guard-controlled waters; most state and local boating laws also require a USCG-approved extinguisher whenever the boat is operated. <PIC> Make sure at least one extinguisher is aboard and full; two are recommended. Check the condition according to the extinguisher manufacturer's instructions. A fire extinguisher is not standard equipment, so obtain one from a boat dealer or fire-extinguisher dealer if needed. <PIC>", ["Manual09_211", "Manual09_212"]

"For throttle-cable care, lubricate the moving parts with water-resistant grease. <PIC> Apply grease to the throttle-cable inner wires at the pulley wheel of the APS, and also grease the steering and shift cable ball joints and inner wires at the jet thrust nozzles as specified. <PIC>", ["Manual09_263", "Manual09_264"]

"Recharging the Battery. Remove the battery cover first, then attach the battery to the charger by aligning the front edge with the mark and sliding it into place. For CG-580, flip out the charger prongs and insert them into a power outlet. <PIC> For CB-5L, connect the power cord to the charger and then to the power outlet; recharging starts automatically and the red lamp starts blinking. A completely exhausted BP-511A or BP-514 takes about 100 minutes, and BP-511 or BP-512 takes about 90 minutes. <PIC> The charger numbers and markings correspond to the charge-status table. <PIC> Do not recharge any battery pack other than Battery Pack BP-511A, BP-514, BP-511, or BP-512. When the camera is not being used for a prolonged period, remove the battery and attach the protective cover to prevent shorting. After the red lamp lights, continue charging for about one hour to attain a full charge. <PIC> You can attach the protective cover in different orientations to indicate whether the battery has been recharged. <PIC> After recharging, detach the battery and unplug the power cord. The charging time varies with ambient temperature and battery level; the battery can operate from 0°C to 40°C, but 10°C to 30°C is recommended for full performance. If operating time becomes sharply reduced even after normal recharging, replace the battery pack. <PIC>", ["Manual10_10", "Manual10_11", "Manual10_12", "Manual10_13", "Manual10_14", "Manual10_15"]

"Installing the camera battery. Load a fully charged BP-511A battery pack. Open the battery compartment cover by sliding the lever in the arrow direction. <PIC> Insert the battery with the contacts facing downward, then push it in until it locks into place. <PIC> Close the cover by pressing it until it snaps shut. <PIC> If a depleted battery is already installed, remove it first by opening the cover and sliding the battery lock lever in the arrow direction before loading the charged battery.", ["Manual10_16", "Camera_09", "Camera_10"]

"Using a household power outlet. Use the optional AC Adapter Kit ACK-E2. First connect the DC Coupler plug to the AC adapter socket. <PIC> Connect the power cord to the AC adapter and insert the plug into a power outlet; when finished, disconnect the plug from the outlet. <PIC> Carefully place the cord in the groove without damaging it. <PIC> Open the battery compartment cover and DC Coupler cord notch cover, insert the DC Coupler until it locks, pass the cord through the notch, and close the cover. Do not connect or disconnect the power cord while the camera power switch is ON. <PIC>", ["Camera_14", "Camera_15", "Manual10_19", "Manual10_20"]

"Mounting a lens. First remove the rear lens cap and the camera body cap by turning them in the direction shown. <PIC> Align an EF-S lens with the white EF-S lens mount index, or align any other EF lens with the red EF lens index mark, then turn the lens in the arrow direction until it clicks into place. <PIC> Set the lens focus mode switch to AF; if it is set to MF, autofocus will not be possible. Then remove the front lens cap. <PIC> When attaching the lens, take care to prevent dust from entering the camera through the lens mount.", ["Manual10_21", "Manual10_22", "Manual10_23"]

"Installing the CF card. Open the CF card slot cover by sliding it in the direction of the arrow. <PIC> Insert the CF card with the label side facing you and the end with the small holes going into the camera; if the card is inserted the wrong way, it may damage the camera. The CF card eject button will pop out when the card is inserted correctly. <PIC> Close the cover and slide it until it snaps shut. <PIC> When the power is turned on, the shots remaining will be displayed on the LCD panel. <PIC> Use a Type I or Type II CF card; the camera is also compatible with Microdrive and CF cards of 2 GB or higher capacity. During card access, do not shake the camera, open the CF card slot cover, or remove the battery.", ["Manual10_25", "Manual10_26", "Manual10_27", "Manual10_28"]

"The manual does not describe removing or disassembling the camera shutter button. It explains how to use the shutter button. The shutter button has two steps: pressing it halfway activates autofocus (AF) and automatic exposure (AE), and the shutter speed/aperture are displayed on the LCD panel and in the viewfinder. <PIC> Pressing it completely releases the shutter and takes the picture. <PIC> If you press it completely without first pressing halfway, or press halfway and then completely immediately, the camera may take a moment before taking the picture. To reduce camera shake, hold the camera steady and press the shutter button gently with your fingertip.", ["Manual10_30", "Manual10_31"]

"Replacing the date/time battery. Turn the camera power switch to OFF, open the battery compartment cover, and remove the main battery. <PIC> Take out the date/time battery holder. <PIC> Replace the battery in the holder with a new CR2016 lithium battery, making sure the + and - orientation is correct. <PIC> Reinstall the holder, close the cover, and set the correct date and time again because the date/time setting is reset after replacement. <PIC>", ["Manual10_46", "Manual10_47", "Manual10_48", "Manual10_49"]

"Focusing an off-center subject. Use focus lock in One-Shot AF. Select a Creative Zone mode and the desired AF point, place that AF point over the subject, and press the shutter button halfway to focus. <PIC> Keep the shutter button pressed halfway while recomposing the picture, then press it completely to take the shot. Focus lock does not work in AI Servo AF or when AI Focus has switched to Servo mode. <PIC>", ["Manual10_106", "Manual10_107"]

"Use the eyepiece cover during self-timer or remote switch operation when your eye does not cover the viewfinder, so stray light will not affect exposure. <PIC> Remove the eyecup by pushing it upward, then slide the eyepiece cover down into the eyepiece groove. <PIC>", ["Manual10_154", "Manual10_155"]

"Selecting the AF Mode. The camera provides three AF modes: One-Shot AF for still subjects, AI Servo AF for moving subjects, and AI Focus AF, which switches from One-Shot AF to AI Servo AF automatically if a still subject starts moving. <PIC> To select the AF mode, press the AF-WB button and, while looking at the LCD panel, turn the Main Dial to choose ONE SHOT, AI FOCUS, or AI SERVO. <PIC> In Basic Zone modes the optimum AF mode is set automatically. If an optional Extender is attached and the maximum aperture of the lens is too small, AF will not be possible. For One-Shot AF, pressing the shutter button halfway activates autofocus once, the AF point that achieves focus flashes, and the focus confirmation light appears; if focus cannot be achieved, the confirmation light blinks and the picture cannot be taken until you recompose and focus again.", ["Camera_30", "Camera_31"]

"Program AE / P mode. Turn the Mode Dial to P to use Program AE; the camera automatically sets the shutter speed and aperture to suit the subject brightness. <PIC> Press the shutter button halfway to focus and check the display. <PIC> Compose and shoot; if the shutter speed and aperture blink, adjust the exposure conditions. <PIC> Program shift is available in P mode: after pressing the shutter button halfway, turn the Main Dial until the desired shutter speed or aperture value appears while keeping the same exposure. Program shift is canceled automatically after the picture is taken and cannot be used with flash. <PIC>", ["Manual10_116", "Manual10_117", "Manual10_118", "Manual10_119"]

"Viewing images on a TV. Open the camera terminal cover and use the provided video cable to connect the camera's video terminal to the TV monitor VIDEO IN terminal; insert the cable plug fully. <PIC> Turn on the TV and switch it to Video IN, set the camera power switch to ON, and press the playback button. The image appears on the TV screen and nothing is displayed on the camera LCD monitor. After finishing, turn both devices off and disconnect the cable; if the image does not display correctly, set the correct video system format. <PIC>", ["Manual10_182", "Manual10_183"]

"To delete a single image from your camera, first display the image you want to erase. <PIC> Then turn the dial to select the image to be erased, and press the button to display the erase menu at the bottom of the screen. <PIC> Finally, turn the dial to select [Erase] and press the button; the access lamp will blink and the image will be erased. If you want to erase other images, repeat the selection steps. <PIC> Note: Once an image is erased, it cannot be recovered. Make sure you no longer need the image before erasing it. To prevent important images from being erased accidentally, protect them.", ["Manual10_184", "Manual10_185", "Manual10_186"]

"Erasing all images. In playback mode, press the erase button to display the erase menu and turn the dial to select All. <PIC> Press SET/confirm; when the confirmation dialog appears, select OK and press SET again. <PIC> All unprotected images are erased. You can cancel while erasing by pressing the indicated button, but erased images cannot be recovered, so protect or transfer important images first. <PIC>", ["Camera_58", "Camera_59", "Manual10_187"]

"CP Direct / Bubble Jet Direct printing. First set the camera communication setting to PTP, turn the camera off, and connect it to the compatible printer using the dedicated interface cable. <PIC> Set up the printer, turn the camera on, and play back the image to print; when the printer connection icon appears, open the print setting screen. <PIC> Choose the print style/options such as paper, borders or date as required. <PIC> Confirm the settings and select OK. <PIC> Press SET to start printing. <PIC> During printing, do not disconnect the cable; use a fully charged battery when the camera is battery-powered. <PIC>", ["Manual10_206", "Manual10_207", "Manual10_208", "Manual10_209", "Manual10_210", "Manual10_211"]

"Custom Functions / fine-tuning camera behavior. Open the menu and select [Custom Functions (C.Fn)]. <PIC> Select the Custom Function number you want to change. <PIC> Choose the setting/description for that Custom Function, such as changing C.Fn-07 Flash firing from 0: Fires to 1: Does not fire, then confirm the setting. <PIC> To return Custom Functions to their defaults, use [Clear all Custom Functions] and select OK. <PIC>", ["Manual10_228", "Camera_75", "Camera_76", "Manual10_229"]

"After opening the package, the main earphone components you should have are the active noise canceling truly wireless earphones themselves. <PIC> You will also find a multifunction button on each earbud. <PIC> The set includes a right earbud and a left earbud. <PIC> There are status LED indicators and battery level LED indicators on the earbuds and charging case. <PIC> Finally, the charging case has a battery level display button to check the case’s remaining power. <PIC>", ["Manual12_0", "Manual12_1", "Manual12_2", "Manual12_3", "Manual12_4"]

"Charging Case Battery Level 1. To power the charging case, insert the USB-C cable into the charging port located at the back of the charging case. <PIC> 2. Insert the standard USB cable into any suitable USB port. <PIC> 3. The Battery Level LED Indicators will light up according to the battery capacity. <PIC> 4. You can see the case battery level at any time by pressing the button on the right hand side of the case. <PIC>", ["earphones_04", "earphones_05", "earphones_06", "earphones_07"]

"Bluetooth pairing/connection scenarios. When the charging case is opened, the earbuds first connect to each other and then enter pairing mode. <PIC> When the earbuds are in the case or removed from it, the LEDs indicate charge or pairing/connection status. <PIC> On the phone, turn Bluetooth on and select the available earphones device; previously paired earbuds may reconnect automatically. For multipoint use, turn Bluetooth off on the first paired device, pair the earbuds to the second device, then turn Bluetooth back on for the first device. <PIC>", ["Manual12_5", "Manual12_6", "Manual12_7"]

"The two main earphone control functions are music control and call control. For music playback, use the music-control button operations shown in the manual to play/pause, change tracks or adjust playback as indicated. <PIC> For phone calls, use the call-control operations to answer, end, reject or otherwise handle calls according to the call-control diagram. <PIC>", ["Manual12_8", "Manual12_9"]

"Other earphone functions besides music and call control. Press and hold until the first beep to activate the phone voice assistant. <PIC> Press and hold in the same way to activate the music app, if supported. <PIC> Press the left earbud to switch Ambient Awareness and ANC modes. <PIC> Press and hold until the second beep to turn Low Latency Mode on or off. <PIC>", ["earphones_01", "earphones_02", "earphones_03", "Manual12_10"]

"Resetting the earbuds. The earbuds must be disconnected from Bluetooth and removed from the case before resetting. For a factory reset, press and hold for 6 seconds; this erases all settings. <PIC> For a hardware reset, press and hold for 10 seconds to restart the earphones, then press again to power them on. <PIC> Hardware reset is only needed if the earbuds lock up or become unresponsive; flashing red and blue lights indicate the reset/connection state described in the manual.", ["Manual12_11", "Manual12_12"]

For maintenance and care, clean the earphones only with a soft cloth or paper towel, and do not use harsh chemicals or detergents. Make sure the earphones are dry before charging. When not in use, store them in a cool, dry place. Do not tug or yank on a cable connected to the charging case; connect and disconnect cables carefully. Avoid exposing the earphones to high temperatures or extreme cold, and recycle or dispose of them according to local rules. The manual also lists key specs such as IP55 sweat/dustproof rating, Bluetooth V5.2, 50 ft Bluetooth range, 60 mAh earbud battery capacity, 600 mAh charging case capacity, about 1 hour earbud charging time, 10 minutes fast charge for about 2 hours playtime, and about 9 hours playtime with up to 36 hours total using the case.

"eReader button and interface layout. FRONT VIEW: [1] Home/ESC cancels a selection or exits to the previous interface; [2] Prev/Next Page opens the previous or next page; [3] Navigation/Menu is a four-way control button and menu/confirm key; [4] Zoom in/out changes JPEG zoom or eBook font size; [5] Rotate switches horizontal/vertical view; [15] TFT LCD Display Screen is the 7-inch display. <PIC> SIDE / BOTTOM INTERFACES: [6] 3.5 mm Earphone Jack connects earphones; [7] USB Port charges the device and connects to a computer for file transfer; [8] Micro SD card reader supports Micro SD/SDHC up to 16 GB; [10] Power button powers the device on/off after pressing 3–5 seconds; [13] Reset On/Off switch restores factory default if a minor problem occurs; [14] Speaker provides 0.5 W audio output. <PIC> NAVIGATION BUTTON VIEW: [9] Play/Pause starts or pauses music/recording; [11] Volume + increases volume; [12] Volume - decreases volume. <PIC>", ["Manual13_0", "Manual13_1", "Manual13_2"]

"Main menu / Browser History. From the main menu, move the navigation keys to select the desired function or file category and press the M button to enter. <PIC> Browser History displays recently browsed files; move the navigation keys to select a book and press M to open it, and the device goes to the last page you read in that book. <PIC> Note: if a file on the Micro SD card has been deleted, its record may remain in Browser History, but it cannot be opened.", ["Manual13_3", "Manual13_4"]

"Page Jump, Save Mark, Load Mark, Del Mark, Browser Mode When in eBook mode, you can press “M” button to enter ”Page Jump”, ”Save Mark”, ”Load Mark”, ”Del Mark”, ”Browser Mode”, ”Flip Time”, ”Brightness”, ”Set color”. <PIC> Page Jump: Press the “M” key then select “page Jump”. Press the “M” button again then key in the desire page number and press “M” to go to that specific page. Bookmarks: This feature allow you to go to certain page of certain book by just selecting it from the bookmark list. Save a bookmark: When in eBook mode, press the ”M” button then select “ save mark” and press “M” again to add the current page as a bookmark. Load a Bookmark: When eBook mode, press ”M” button then select ”Load Mark ” and press “M” again to open the saved bookmark list. Select the desire bookmark and press “M” key. Delete a bookmark: When eBook mode, press the ”M” button then select ”Del mark”; a list of saved bookmark will pop out. Please select the one you wish to delete then press “M” key to confirm. Bookmark capacity : This device allow up to 8 saved bookmark. When it reach its limit, the newly saved bookmark will overwrite the oldest bookmark. Zoom: Press this key to change the font size. There are 3 different font size: Small, Medium and Large. Rotate: When in eBook mode, you can rotate the screen either horizontally or vertically for your convenience by pressing this rotate button. Browser Mode : There are two browser: ”Auto Mode” and “Manual Mode”. Flip Time: There are five flip time to select: 10Sec, 15Sec, 20Sec, 25Sec, 30Sec. Brightness: There are five level brightness to select, you can select the desire comfortable brightness. Set Color: There are five colors to select, you can select the comfortable color word to read.", ["eReader_08"]

"Music mode. Open the audio file list from the main menu, select the desired audio file, and press the M button to enter play mode. You can add audio files by connecting the eReader to a computer with the USB cable, then dragging and copying audio files into the device. The manual lists supported audio formats such as MP3 and WMA, and allows music playback while reading an eBook or browsing photos/menus. <PIC> During playback, use Up/Down or page keys to adjust volume, Play/Pause to pause or continue, hold the left/right direction keys to rewind or fast-forward, and press left/right briefly for previous or next audio file. Press M in Music mode to adjust Repeat Mode, Play Mode, EQ settings, and related music-play modes. <PIC>", ["Manual13_7", "Manual13_8"]

"Voice Recording Select the ”Record” in the main menu, click ”M” button to enter the voice record mode. <PIC> How to start the Recording: Press the ”Play/Pause” button to start the recording, press it again to pause the recording, press the ”HOME” to stop the recording. After you done with the recording you will be prompted to ask if want to save into the device. Please select “YES” or “NOT” by pressing the “M” key. <PIC> Record Playback Function: 1. Go to main menu and select “Music”, press “M” to go to “Musci Menu”. 2. Select ”Record” and press the ”M” button to go to “Recorded” file list. 3. Select the desire recorded file then press “M” to start playback.", ["Manual13_11", "Manual13_12"]

"Video Go to “Video” and press “M” key to enter the Video mode. This device AVI, RMVB and MPEG2 video format. <PIC> Subtitle language: When in video playing mode. If subtitles are available from your video file, press the ”M” button then press Subtitle Language to make change. Select Time play: Press the ”M” button then select “time play”, you can change the time to play. Full screen: Press the ”M” button then select “Full Screen” to change the screen display. There are three mode: “Full screen”, “Normal” and “Original”. Brightness: There are five level of brightness, you can select the comfortable brightness.", ["Manual13_9"]

"Photo viewer. Yes, the eReader can display photos. Go to Photo and press the M button to enter Photo mode; the device supports JPEG and BMP image formats. <PIC> Use the left/right navigation keys for previous/next photo, press Play/Pause to rotate the photo counterclockwise, and use the zoom keys to zoom in or out. Large image files may take longer to rotate and load than small files.", ["Manual13_10"]

Troubleshooting for the eReader includes these common problems and solutions: If it cannot power on, charge the device until the power indicator bar is full; if it still fails, contact the manufacturer. If it cannot charge, check for a defective AC adaptor or USB cable and contact the manufacturer for replacement. If there is no sound or noise through earphones, adjust the volume, try another pair of earphones, and make sure the music file quality/compression rate is adequate. If files cannot be downloaded, check the USB cable, available memory, and whether the computer needs a USB 2.0 driver. If music files cannot play, the format or resolution may not be supported, so contact technical support.

"Fax connection / telephone line safety. Place the product near a telephone wall jack and a standard grounded AC power outlet. For fax models, use caution when installing or modifying telephone lines; never handle telephone wiring during a thunderstorm and never install a telephone wall jack in a wet location. <PIC> The product may be safely connected to the telephone line with a standard modular jack, USOC RJ11C; the plug and jack used for premises wiring and the telephone network must comply with FCC Part 68/ACTA requirements. Before accessing the inside of the product, unplug the telephone line cord first, then unplug the power cord. <PIC>", ["Manual15_2", "Manual15_3"]

"Fax safety precautions. For models with the fax function, follow basic telephone-equipment safety precautions to reduce the risk of fire, electric shock and injury: read and save all instructions. <PIC> Do not use the product near water or in wet locations, such as near a bathtub, wash bowl, kitchen sink, washing machine, wet basement or swimming pool. <PIC> Avoid using the product during a thunderstorm because there may be a remote risk of electric shock from lightning. <PIC> Do not use the product to report a gas leak in the vicinity of the leak. <PIC> Use only the power cord provided with the product, if it is included in the box. <PIC> Pay attention to the warning and caution symbols shown in the safety guide before using or servicing the fax. <PIC> Follow the safety markings and product labels rather than removing or ignoring them. <PIC> Keep the safety instructions for later reference. <PIC>", ["fax_01", "fax_02", "fax_03", "fax_04", "fax_05", "fax_06", "fax_07", "Manual15_1"]

"Finger-safety cautions for the fax. Wait until pages have exited the product before picking them up; otherwise your fingers may be trapped inside the machine. Do not put your hand or foreign objects into the ink insertion slot. If the tray has been extended for large paper, position the product so the tray does not protrude past the edge of the desk or table. <PIC> To prevent injury, do not put your fingers in the illustrated areas of the product. <PIC> When changing the tray size from the large paper size back to the original size, do not pinch your fingers in the gaps or slots at the bottom of the tray. <PIC> On the listed MFC models, keep your fingers away from the additional illustrated pinch points. <PIC>", ["Manual15_6", "Manual15_7", "Manual15_8", "Manual15_9"]

"Moving the fax. Before moving it, turn the product off, unplug the power cord and telephone/network cables, and remove loose items. <PIC> For larger models, at least two people should lift it: one holding the front and the other holding the back. <PIC> Carry it by sliding your hands into the handhold indentations on each side; do not carry it by holding the scanner cover, and keep the product level so ink does not spill. <PIC> When putting it down, be careful not to trap your fingers. <PIC>", ["fax_08", "Manual15_10", "Manual15_11", "Manual15_12"]

"Yes. The caution and warning labels inside the fax/printer are important and must not be removed or damaged. They mark hazards such as moving parts, electrical shock, fire risk, finger-pinch areas and other product-specific safety precautions. <PIC> Keep all warnings and instructions marked on the product, and follow the labels during use, cleaning, maintenance, moving and paper-tray operation. <PIC>", ["Manual15_14", "Manual15_15"]

For Canada, the manual includes an Industry Canada Compliance Statement: the device complies with Industry Canada licence-exempt RSSs and operates under two conditions: it may not cause interference, and it must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.
